messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: list names in l*ply
parts:
hello group-

this simple thing has bothered me for a while. i want to be able to get the name of a list entry within the function in a l*ply call, e.g.

a.list <- list( a=1:10, b=45:90)
laply( a.list, function(li) { names(li); sum(li) } )

I want it to print "a" and then "b" and I dont care that llply would bequeath the names onto the output list. i'd either like the name of  the index in a.list[[i]] so i could get the names(a.list)[i]. 

hoping you're more clever than I on this one.

James

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: list names in l*ply
parts:
Two options:

* iterate on the index:
laply(seq_along(a.list), function(i) { names(a.list)[i]; sum(a.list[[i]]) } )

* use maply
maply(cbind(a.list, names(a.list)), function(x, nm) {...} )

Hadley

messages.author: 0a86bb0ca38ae4f0
messages.subject: Re: list names in l*ply
parts:
Here's another option that I've recently been using--creating each
name as an attribute, so now it resides inside the object.
library(plyr)# define a function to add the name of each element of a
list as an attribute to that element. i/p=list, o/p=list with attr's
addedaddNameAttr<-function(myList,name="Name") {  for (i in
seq_along(myList)) attr(myList[[i]],name)<-names(myList)[i]  myList}
# define extraction function to get the name of an element of the
listgetNameAttr<-function(x,name="Name") attr(x,name)
# Example# define a list with namestest<-
list(firstEntry=data.frame(y=runif(10),x=runif(10)),secondEntry=data.frame(y=runif(10),x=runif(10)))#
add names as attributestest<-addNameAttr(test)# use idea to access
names in l_plywindows(6,3)par(mfrow=c(1,2))l_ply(test,function(z)
plot(y~x,z,main=getNameAttr(z)))
This let's you use l*ply in its natural form.
